status: Proposed component claim, not default-branch acceptance or learner attainment
claimKind: conceptual knowledge of the declared four-component model

reuseDecision.lifestyleClaims: Complete lifestyle/benefit explanations can say exercise helps heart, muscles and mental health while still treating one strong effort and repeated muscular effort as the same capacity or confusing flexibility with speed.
reuseDecision.bonesAndHeart: Anatomical structure/pumping and oxygen-delivery knowledge does not distinguish the four fitness capacities or select an activity for a specified capacity.
reuseDecision.preparation: The complete actual warm-up/mobility operation can be performed without classifying strength versus endurance or whole-body stamina.
reuseDecision.goalSetting: The full plan/monitor/adjust operation does not supply these specific physiological capacity distinctions.

independentWitness.oldClaimsCanSucceed: Explain circulation and muscle/bone movement, perform a suitable warm-up and mobility sequence, describe exercise/diet/drug benefits and risks, and complete a realistic personal goal. Still call every long/repeated activity strength and treat a flexible-looking body as globally fitter.
independentWitness.newClaimCanSucceed: Accurately distinguish the four capacities using supplied activity conditions and new goal cases, acknowledge overlap and reject appearance-based inference without having to perform a maximal strength/endurance test or explain four heart chambers.

remainingCurriculumTasks.ON-HPE-2019-G6-B2.3: Actual safe self-assessment across the relevant capacities and comparable observations over time. A conceptual answer is not the performance record.
remainingCurriculumTasks.ON-HPE-2019-G6-B2.4: Implement and review an interest-based plan using the relevant assessment information. Naming capacities is not implementation.

guideStatus: Original untested low-confidence design; public primary resources support the definitions, not efficacy of these lessons.
